_what: Authored copy and timing for the silent mission pause and the underwater closing passage.

pause._black_hold: 30 frames, DOWN FROM 89 and no longer tied to gap_frames (see `_pacing`; the gap is 48). The long hold existed because the asteroid impact followed the passage directly and the film wanted it to break the silence out of darkness. After the 2026-08-16 reorder the passage is followed by movement 5a instead -- a dark Earth limb that is itself near-black for 3.504 s. 89 frames of black in front of that made roughly five seconds of unbroken dark and buried the song's re-entry. The half second left is only enough for the last card to clear before the music arrives, which is what 'kick them with the boom' needs: the cards breathe, the black does not.
pause._retired_card: 'Left to teach' (240 frames, renders/artwork/huntress.png) was REMOVED from the pause on 2026-08-23 at the owner's word: "remove the 'left to teach' slide". Recorded rather than deleted, because a retired string is authored copy too and re-seating it anywhere is then a move rather than a rewrite.
pause._pacing: Owner 2026-08-23: "lengthen the slide intervals, this is a dramatic moment. Then kick them with the boom!" Both intervals grew. The gap between cards went 30 -> 48 frames (0.5 -> 0.8 s), and every remaining card gained 60 frames of hold (mission 300->360, we-are 240->300, purpose 240->300, lesson 210->270), because at fade_frames=72 a 240-frame card sat at full brightness for only 1.6 s and the 210-frame `lesson` for 1.1 s -- the fades, not the holds, were most of the card. black_hold_frames is DELIBERATELY LEFT AT 30 and no longer matches gap_frames: it is the run-up to the impact, and the reason it is short is in `_black_hold`. Dropping a card and lengthening what is left lands within half a second of the old 23.023 s.

underwater._window: source_in is still the underwater pullback's first frame. source_out moved 427.44 -> 499.300 on 2026-08-16 because the passage grew past the pullback: the owner seated two centre cards in the long tail after it -- 'Fight for Us' on the ocean wide and 'For Nóva' on the sunken hull. 499.300 is the megacut's own out point for this clip (trim_to 109.5, plus the 389.800 in point), so the section describes exactly the picture the programme plays. active_y/active_height still describe the scope letterbox every bottom_matte card sits in; that has not changed.

This section was originally shorted, lengthen it a bit for dramatic purposes for a few seconds before going into the credits', and their answer on HOW: hold it longer on the picture that is already there. 28:20 is 108.46 on this clock and the passage ends at 109.5, which is one second of card. RUNNING PAST 109.5 IS RULED OUT BY MEASUREMENT, not by preference: the source's own burned credits ('(c) A LOVELY BUNCH OF COCONUTS 2024 / DIRECTED BY VILLE LIPIAINEN') fade in from 111.0 and are readable by 111.5. So the card comes UP EARLIER instead, at 106.0, and holds 3.5 s to the out point -- three and a half times the screen time, no new picture, and no risk of somebody else's credit under ours. It plays over the sunken hull interior, measured at YAVG 24-30 and falling, which is the darkest bed in the passage.

The mark is the Kubernetes wheel from cncf/artwork, cached by scripts/fetch_brand_marks.py at renders/marks/kubernetes.png and credited in ATTRIBUTIONS.md (CC BY 4.0; it is also a Linux Foundation trademark). IT IS REPRODUCED AS DRAWN AND IS NOT RECOLOURED: the sear is on the ACUTE ACCENT above it, which is ours, not on somebody else's mark -- the same line the trailer's KubeCon card draws when it sears its divider and leaves the wordmark alone. The glyph sits at 0.86em on the text baseline so it reads as the letter it stands in for rather than as a logo dropped into a word.
